processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Steel ingot fabricated by VIM was homogenized at 1200 °C for 4 h prior to hot forging; upstream step of the tested steel's route.
Hot forged to a thickness of 40 mm followed by air cooling to room temperature (parent forging route).
Specimen placed in a box furnace, heated to 850 °C and held for 2 h before rolling (sample named R850).
Hot rolling deformation with a 60 % reduction ratio, reducing plate thickness from 40 mm to 16 mm.
After rolling the sample was air cooled to room temperature.

structures.overall_structure: Duplex lamellar (banded) structure of light δ-ferrite lamellae alternating with dark honeycomb martensite lamellae; numerous equiaxed ferrite grains formed by DIFT (DIF) are enclosed within the honeycomb martensite lamellae. Spherical carbides are completely dissolved at this rolling temperature.

phases_present.morphology: dark honeycomb lamellae enclosing equiaxed ferrite grains
equiaxed grains enclosed within honeycomb martensite lamellae (submicron level)

defects.type: equiaxed DIF grains acting as pre-existing defects / crack propagation shortcuts

grain_structure.texture: Dominant orientation shifts from <001> (low-temperature rolling zone) to <101> in the high-temperature rolling zone (R850/R950).

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Significant hardness differences between martensite (5.98–6.50 GPa), DIF (2.84–2.98 GPa) and δ-ferrite (2.64–2.77 GPa) weaken phase-interface bonding and concentrate stress at the crack tip; the maximum hardness difference in the high-temperature rolling zone reaches 3.86 GPa. These interfaces become preferential crack-initiation sites.
Equiaxed DIF grains enclosed in honeycomb martensite lamellae act as pre-existing defects, guiding cracks to propagate rapidly in a cleavage mode and significantly reducing energy consumption.

interfaces.phase_evolution: At the 850 °C high-temperature rolling condition carbides dissolve completely; the δ+γ two-phase region stabilizes austenite and promotes carbide dissolution, and after rolling residual austenite transforms to martensite, with DIFT producing equiaxed ferrite grains surrounded by martensite.
interfaces.interface_notes: The δ-ferrite/martensite phase-boundary hardness mismatch and the DIF 'crack propagation shortcut' jointly cause brittle fracture in this high-temperature-rolled sample.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: Tensile: rod-shaped, gauge length 25 mm, diameter 5 mm, sampled along RD; Charpy impact: V-notch bars 10 mm × 10 mm × 55 mm, notch on rolled surface, impact direction perpendicular to RD

fracture_toughness.value: 5.6 ± 0.6 J (Charpy V-notch impact absorption energy, IAE)

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Charpy impact absorption energy (IAE) and total elongation

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Optical microscope; image analysis with Image-J software; samples etched with 5 vol% HNO3-ethanol
characterization_methods.purpose: Reveal the lamellar macrostructure and quantify M, δ-F and C/F proportions
characterization_methods.key_findings: R850 shows alternating δ-ferrite (light) and honeycomb martensite (dark) lamellae with equiaxed ferrite grains enclosed in the martensite; M = 33.2 ± 3.6 vol%, δ-F = 66.8 ± 3.6 vol%, C/F = 0.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Apreo S HiVac SEM with Oxford Aztec EBSD detector; RD-ND plane
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: RD-ND plane, etched with 5 vol% HNO3-ethanol
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize the lamellar/honeycomb morphology and carbide distribution
characterization_methods.key_findings: Honeycomb-like morphology labelled δ-ferrite (upper), martensite (middle) and ferrite (arrowed); no spherical carbide contrast (carbides dissolved).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Apreo S HiVac SEM equipped with Oxford Aztec EBSD detector; electro-polished with 5 vol% HClO4-ethanol
characterization_methods.purpose: Quantify GB character (HAGB), KAM, GOS, texture and dislocation density
characterization_methods.key_findings: R850: HAGBs 60.1 %, GOS≤2° 19.4 %, dislocation density 2.1 × 10^14 m-2, KAM 0.3–0.4°; IPF shows coarse, more equiaxed multi-coloured grains with lamellar remnants.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JEM-F200 (CF-HR) TEM; specimens ground to 80 µm, punched into 3 mm discs, twin-jet electropolished in 5 vol% HClO4-acetic acid
characterization_methods.purpose: High-resolution microstructure observation of phases and secondary phases
characterization_methods.key_findings: R850 shows light equiaxed ferrite grains embedded in martensite with internal dislocation structure; no spherical carbides present.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: G200X nanoindenter, peak load 5 mN, loading/unloading rate 500 µN/s, Oliver-Pharr method; indentation positions validated by EBSD
characterization_methods.key_findings: R850: martensite 6.0 ± 0.5 GPa, ferrite 2.6 ± 0.3 GPa, DIF 3.0 ± 0.3 GPa.

characterization_methods.technique: Tensile testing and Charpy V-notch impact testing
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Tensile: rod-shaped specimen (gauge 25 mm, dia 5 mm), crosshead speed 1.5 mm/min; Charpy V-notch bars 10 mm × 10 mm × 55 mm, notch on rolled surface
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Room temperature; tensile along RD; impact direction perpendicular to RD
characterization_methods.key_findings: R850: UTS 1160.0 ± 15.4 MPa, TE 8.3 ± 0.1 %, IAE 5.6 ± 0.6 J, with Ei = 3.91 J and Ep = 2.10 J showing an unstable single-peak brittle impact curve.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Equilibrium phase diagram and phase composition determined at each temperature for the tested steel composition
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Predicted carbide stability range (≤750 °C) is consistent with the observed retained carbide/ferrite composite lamellae at low rolling temperature and complete carbide dissolution at 850 °C.

analytical_models.equation_role: Explains dislocation pinning by carbides (applicable to the carbide-containing low-temperature-rolled samples rather than R850)
analytical_models.model_note: In the low-temperature rolling zone, carbide particles pin dislocations via the Orowan mechanism; not active in the carbide-free R850 sample.

analytical_models.equation_role: ρ = 2θ/(µb) used to calculate dislocation density from average KAM value θ, step size µ and Burgers vector b
analytical_models.model_note: Applied to EBSD KAM data to obtain the dislocation density reported for R850 (2.1 × 10^14 m-2).

unmapped_findings: R850 strength–plasticity product (SPP = Rm × A) is 9.6 ± 0.1 GPa% (Table 4).

R850 instrumented Charpy impact: crack initiation energy Ei = 3.91 J and crack propagation energy Ep = 2.10 J (Fig. 5c), with a steep single impact-load peak (~17 kN) that decays within about 1 mm of displacement.
R850 EBSD: HAGB fraction 60.1 % and fraction of grains with GOS ≤ 2° = 19.4 % (Table 3 / Fig. 4c,g,k,o).
R850 work-hardening rate (θ) curve decreases monotonically with true strain without a hump, extending to about 0.08 true strain (Fig. 5f), indicating lack of coordinated multi-phase deformation.
R850 room-temperature impact energy is essentially zero (~5 J) in Fig. 5a, consistent with the tabulated IAE of 5.6 ± 0.6 J.

In the high-temperature rolling zone (R850/R950) the maximum phase nano-hardness difference reaches 3.86 GPa (martensite 5.98–6.50 GPa > DIF 2.84–2.98 GPa > δ-ferrite 2.64–2.77 GPa), which is larger than the abstract's stated >3.3 GPa martensite/ferrite difference.
Thermo-Calc predicts carbides vanish (dissolve to zero fraction) at about 710 °C, explaining the complete carbide dissolution in the R850 sample rolled at 850 °C.
